name: Airbnb
summary: Airbnb's interviews are known for pairing technical or craft rounds with interviews about its core values, which it publishes: Champion the Mission, Be a Host, Embrace the Adventure and Be a Cereal Entrepreneur. Candidates commonly report a recruiter call, a technical screen, and a final loop of coding or craft interviews plus one or two values interviews, often with people from outside the hiring team.
rounds: Technical or craft screen (for engineers, often a live coding interview)
Final loop: coding, system design for experienced roles, and a past-project deep dive
One or two core values interviews, often with someone from another team
For some roles, a test, a recorded video or an event, as Airbnb's careers FAQ notes
looks_for: Understanding of hosts and guests and the trust between them
Clean, working code and clear communication

questions.text: Tell me about a time you went out of your way to make someone feel welcome or supported at work.
covers: Who it was and what they needed
What you did, specifically
The difference it made to them and to the team

questions.text: Tell me about a time you turned a bold idea into something real with limited resources.
covers: The idea and why it seemed unlikely
How you got creative with little time, money or help
What you built and what happened next

questions.text: Tell me about a setback you bounced back from. What did it teach you?
covers: What went wrong and how it felt, honestly
What you did to recover
How it changed the way you work or think

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to build trust between two groups who wanted different things.
covers: The two groups and what each wanted
How you understood both sides before proposing anything
The agreement you reached and how trust held up afterwards

questions.text: How would you design search for stays, so guests can filter by place, dates and price and still get results quickly?
covers: Location search, then checking availability for the dates
Indexes and caching, and which filters are costly
Ranking results and keeping availability accurate

questions.text: How would you design a booking system that stops two guests reserving the same home for the same night?
covers: Modelling availability by night for each listing
Locking or a database constraint, so only one booking wins
Handling payment failures, holds that expire, and hosts' calendars synced elsewhere

questions.text: How would you help guests and hosts trust each other before a first booking? Talk me through product and technical ideas.
covers: What each side worries about
Ideas such as verification, reviews, clear rules and messaging
How you'd measure whether trust improved

questions.text: After a release, prices for stays in one city look wrong. How would you investigate?
covers: Confirming the scope and comparing with prices before the release
Checking currency, taxes, fees and city-specific rules in the change
Rolling back if guests are affected, then fixing and adding a test

questions.text: How would you support many languages and currencies in one app?
covers: Keeping text out of code, with translation files and right-to-left layouts
Storing money with its currency and converting only for display
Dates, number formats and testing in several locales

questions.text: Walk me through a project you're proud of: the problem, your design and what you'd change.
covers: The problem and who it was for
Your design and one hard trade-off
What you'd change now

questions.text: Why Airbnb? Tell me about a trip or stay, yours or someone else's, that shaped how you see the product.
covers: A real, specific experience
What it showed you about guests, hosts or belonging
How it connects to the work you'd do

questions.text: Which Airbnb core value is closest to how you work, and when have you shown it?
covers: One value, named once
A short, true story
Why that value matters to you

questions.text: What does belonging mean to you, at work or when you travel?
covers: A personal, specific answer rather than a definition
A moment you felt you belonged, or didn't
How you help others feel it

tips: Prepare true, personal stories for the core values interviews; candidates commonly describe them as conversations about who you are, not only your work.
Use the product as a guest and read how hosting works, so you can talk about both sides of the marketplace.
In coding rounds, aim for code that runs and talk through edge cases as you go.
Read your interview invitation carefully: Airbnb's careers FAQ says some roles involve a test, a video or an event.
